description: Three-panel composite of optical micrographs of as-quenched low-density Fe–18Mn–10Al–xC steels. Each panel carries a lowercase letter label (a, b, c) at the top left and a black 40 µm scale bar at the bottom right; no other annotations, axis or numeric labels are printed. (a) 0.5C steel: strongly banded duplex structure in which dark-grey, elongated and discontinuous second-phase bands lie roughly horizontally inside a lighter grey matrix; grain boundaries are visible within the light regions. (b) 0.8C steel: the same duplex character but markedly finer and more mottled/equiaxed — the light-grey phase appears as smaller, more isolated islands dispersed through the darker matrix, and the banding is far weaker than in (a). (c) 1.2C steel: coarse equiaxed polygonal grains of a single matrix phase, many grains traversed by straight, parallel-sided annealing twins occurring as single or multiple sets. Together the panels show that raising C from 0.5 to 0.8 wt% refines the duplex structure and that the 1.2C steel is fully austenitic with annealing twins; the citing text gives austenite fractions of 59.2% and 84.8% for the 0.5C and 0.8C steels, values that are not printed on the figure.

observations.observation: The figure is a three-panel set of optical micrographs labelled a, b, c, each bearing a black 40 µm scale bar at the bottom right.
Panel (a) shows a banded structure: dark-grey elongated, discontinuous bands aligned roughly horizontally within a lighter grey matrix, with grain boundaries visible in the light regions.

Panel (b) shows a distinctly finer and more equiaxed/mottled structure than (a), in which the light-grey phase forms small isolated islands dispersed in the darker matrix; banding is much less pronounced.
Panel (c) shows coarse equiaxed polygonal grains containing straight, parallel-sided annealing twins, often as multiple parallel sets within one grain.
No phase labels, volume-fraction values or other numeric annotations are printed on any of the three micrographs; the only printed measure is the 40 µm scale bar.
The caption states that the panels are optical microstructures of Fe–18Mn–10Al–xC steels, with (a) 0.5C steel, (b) 0.8C steel and (c) 1.2C steel.
The citing text states that the microstructures are of the as-quenched steels.

The citing text states that the 0.5C and 0.8C steels have a duplex ferritic–austenitic microstructure, whereas the banded vs island morphology seen in (a) and (b) is not labelled with phase names in the pixels.
The citing text states that the 1.2C steel is fully austenitic with some annealing twins in grains, which is consistent with the twinned polygonal grain structure seen in panel (c).
The citing text reports austenite volume fractions determined to be 59.2% and 84.8% in the 0.5C and 0.8C steels respectively; these numbers are not printed on the figure.

subfigures.description: Optical micrograph of the 0.5C steel, 40 µm scale bar: dark-grey elongated, discontinuous bands aligned roughly horizontally in a lighter grey matrix, i.e. a banded duplex structure with visible grain boundaries in the light regions.

Optical micrograph of the 0.8C steel, 40 µm scale bar: a finer, more equiaxed/mottled duplex structure with light-grey phase as small isolated islands in a darker matrix; banding much weaker than in (a).
Optical micrograph of the 1.2C steel, 40 µm scale bar: coarse equiaxed polygonal grains with abundant straight, parallel-sided annealing twins crossing individual grains.

unreadable_items: No phase labels are printed on panels (a) and (b), so the light/dark contrast cannot be assigned to ferrite vs austenite from the pixels alone
